evidence.statement: A 24-bp exact block TAAGGTAGCGAAATTCCTTGTCGG occurs five times in the frozen E. coli genome and once in the frozen Pyrococcus genome; no full-block yeast occurrence was reported.
Post-freeze annotation identifies this exact 24-base sequence as Uni23S1926F, a published primer sequence used to amplify bacterial 23S rRNA.
Treat this as a 23S-rRNA-associated conserved primitive; the primer match validates sequence identity/location but is not itself a claim that the genomic segment's natural role is 'primer'.
LC-PRIM-0002 begins four bases before LC-PRIM-0003, mapping it to E. coli 23S positions 1926-1949; this independently agrees with its published Uni23S1926F designation.

unknowns: Specific molecular contribution of the full 24-bp exact sequence beyond its validated 23S-rRNA association.
